- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for volatility.  
- After a recent spike in price, model frequently overshoots in the following 3–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–8% from forecast for 5–10 days post-spike.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75% of recent high), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of recent low.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a “first 7 days” downward bias of 3–7% to reflect initial overconfidence.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.6, 0.2, 0.8), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
